notes: LOCKED, left alone: the Changes tab (data-cd-id="changes", data-cd-locked) has class "tab". maude-v2 has no .tabbar/.tab; it switches views with its segmented control (.seg + aria-pressed). I didn't touch the tab bar, so it stays half-converted until a person unlocks that button (⇧⌘L). Then the .tabbar/.tab pair can become .seg, with aria-pressed alongside aria-selected.

GitPanel.css is a sibling file, not part of this canvas edit. After the switch, run `maude design ds-check --fix=mechanical --canvas ui/panels/GitPanel.tsx` to apply the S2 aliases it reports: --canvas-bg/--canvas-dot/--canvas-grid → --x-canvas-*, --accent-muted → --accent-soft, --accent-tint → --selection. It also needs a .gp-callout-warn rule (background: var(--bg-3); plus a warn icon in --status-warn-text) to replace callout--warn.

GitPanel.css says .callout is 'row-flex with a left accent bar' (line 401). The v2 callout has no accent bar, so the Get-latest nudge and the conflict callout will look flatter. Check them in the screenshot after applying.

Already-existing ds-check warnings, not caused by the switch: literal font-weight: 600, font-size: 10px, gap: 5px, margin-left: -6px in GitPanel.css, plus 15 more. v2 has --weight-semibold and the --type-* ladder for these.

DECISION — layout: maude-v2's hard rule is 'Chrome floats; it never frames', with a docked layout only as an Advanced option. Every artboard here is a full-height docked side panel plus a menubar. The class swap keeps that layout. Moving it onto a floating .island is a redesign, not a switch.

DECISION — words: v2 says no developer chrome in the default view (no branch names, no paths). The menubar shows 'maude / main' and each file row shows a path such as ui/Pricing v3.tsx. One row points at system/maude/preview/components-cards.tsx, the old system. Decide whether these move behind an Advanced section.

DECISION — colour roles: the avatars use --accent ('YO') and --status-info ('RY') as hues. In v2, azure is for actions only and status colours always come with a word, so --presence-* would be the fit. The M/A/D/U badges are a local .gp-badge; v2 marks status with .chip, which you may want to adopt.

DECISION — theme and mark: data-theme stays dark. Light is v2's default and dark has equal status, so either works. The local <Mark> draws its own spark-on-bubble. v2 asks for the mark lifted verbatim from system/maude-v2/assets/logos.
meta.json: only designSystem changes, maude → maude-v2. opt_out_scope "palette" stays as it is.
